text:
Recent research confirms that sampled-candidate evaluation can change model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation; exposure bias further complicates both. RecSys 2025 evaluates sampling through resolution, fidelity, robustness, and predictive power ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086)). For this task, retain pinned sampled HR@10 as the selection objective; use full-catalog target ranks and model-order agreement as supplementary diagnostics. Full-catalog ranking still measures agreement with observed interactions, not complete user preferences. The 2024 popularity-bias survey supports inspecting differences across users and item popularity ([survey](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11257-024-09406-0)). Practical slices: training-frequency bins and history-length bins, with counts and per-category results.

Recommended uncertainty analysis: paired user-level bootstrap within each category, recomputing the equally weighted four-category HR@10 difference each replicate. Preserve candidate sets and pair users across models. These intervals describe evaluation-sample uncertainty conditional on trained models; they do not capture training-seed variation or correct adaptive model selection. Repeated validation reuse can overfit the holdout, as established by [adaptive-data-analysis research](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629). Log every trial, predefine diagnostic interpretations, and avoid treating tiny validation gains as established improvements. Twenty qualitative users support case analysis, not population-level claims or inferred diversity/conformity traits.

Proposed fault-injection checks: positive score rescaling should preserve ranks despite changing margins; random scores should yield expected sampled HR@10 of 0.10 with 100 candidates and unbiased tie handling. History shuffling, truncation, and popularity-only scoring can reveal sequence dependence and popularity shortcuts, although degradation is an empirical question. Calibrate probe responses against observed HR@10 changes. These are proposed engineering checks, consistent with the broader [2024 robustness-evaluation literature](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.17844), rather than a validated diagnostic suite.
